title: The Sunday Read: ‘I’ve Always Struggled With My Weight. Losing It Didn’t Mean Winning.’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 Dealbook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: We are hopefully at the semi-end of a giant global pandemic, and in all the huge swirl of emotions that comes with that pandemic, I've been having a lot of feelings lately about
sentences.zh: 我们大概正处于一场全球性大流行的尾声，在随之而来的各种复杂情绪中，我最近对

sentences.en: my weight and my body.
sentences.zh: 我的体重和身体产生了很多感触。

sentences.en: It's like a lot of people, I put on some serious pounds during quarantine.
sentences.zh: 和很多人一样，我在隔离期间胖了不少。

sentences.en: Stress eating snacks, some glasses of wine.
sentences.zh: 压力性进食零食，喝了几杯红酒。

sentences.en: I remember near the beginning, there were jokes about the
sentences.zh: 我记得刚开始的时候，大家都在开玩笑说

sentences.en: COVID-19, the 19 pounds that people gained in quarantine.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情，也就是人们在隔离期间增加的19磅体重。

sentences.en: Mine was significantly more than that.
sentences.zh: 我增加的远不止这些。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, I started to feel pretty bad about it and decided to try to lose that weight.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我开始为此感到非常糟糕，于是决定尝试减肥。

sentences.en: My name is Sam Anderson, and I'm a staff writer for the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫萨姆·安德森，是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: I was talking to my editor on the phone about all this recently.
sentences.zh: 最近我还在电话里和编辑聊起过这些事。

sentences.en: Just casually, hey, you know, I actually lost my pandemic weight using a weight loss app recently, and I feel really silly about it.
sentences.zh: 就是随口一提，嘿，你知道吗，我最近其实用减肥软件减掉了疫情期间增加的体重，我觉得这事儿挺傻的。

sentences.en: And I have mixed feelings about this whole process.
sentences.zh: 我对整个过程心情复杂。

sentences.en: And she said, oh, you have to write an essay about this.
sentences.zh: 她说，哦，你一定要写一篇关于这个的文章。

sentences.en: And that made me really think about my relationship to my body and the danger of diet culture, but also the self-esteem that gets wrapped up in how our bodies
sentences.zh: 这让我开始认真思考我与自己身体的关系，以及节食文化的危险，还有那些包裹在我们身体外表上的自尊心，

sentences.en: look and what losing weight really means and if it changes anything about you as a person.
sentences.zh: 以及减肥到底意味着什么，它是否会改变作为一个人的你。

sentences.en: So I'm going to share a piece I wrote for the New York Times Magazine health issue
sentences.zh: 所以，我打算分享一篇我为《纽约时报杂志》健康专刊写的内容，

sentences.en: about gaining weight and losing weight and just what it means to be a human being walking around in a meat suit all the time.
sentences.zh: 关于增重和减肥，以及作为一个终日行走在皮囊之中的人类究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: There were a few bad moments over the course of a few bad months that led me to download the weight loss app.
sentences.zh: 在过去几个糟糕的月份里，有几个糟糕的时刻促使我下载了那个减肥软件。

sentences.en: These will probably sound trivial to anyone who is not me.
sentences.zh: 对别人来说，这些可能听起来微不足道。

sentences.en: And of course, they are trivial.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们确实微不足道。

sentences.en: But we are talking about bodies here and about my body in particular.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在谈论的是身体，特别是我的身体。

sentences.en: And one of the defining features of having a body is that it is a fire hose of tiny
sentences.zh: 拥有身体的一个显著特征就是，它就像一根不断喷射着细小

sentences.en: humiliations blasting you constantly in the face, never allowing you to look away, even when you most want to.
sentences.zh: 羞辱的消防水管，时刻对着你的脸喷射，让你无法移开视线，即使你最想逃避的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: One bad moment happened in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 其中一个糟糕的时刻发生在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: I had flown out during a lull in the pandemic to visit my great friend Alan, a friend so close he is basically a reflection of my own soul.
sentences.zh: 在疫情的间隙，我飞去探望我的挚友艾伦，他和我亲密到几乎是我灵魂的倒影。

sentences.en: And as Alan and I wrapped each other in a big hug of ecstatic reunion, he suddenly reached down to my waist and playfully pinched my love handles.
sentences.zh: 当艾伦和我紧紧拥抱，沉浸在重逢的狂喜中时，他突然伸手向下，戏谑地捏了捏我的腰间赘肉。

sentences.en: Probed them in the way a fishmonger might assess a large hunk of priceless tuna.
sentences.zh: 那动作就像鱼贩在评估一块昂贵的金枪鱼肉。

sentences.en: And he said, what happened here?
sentences.zh: 他说，这儿是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Did you eat my friend Sam?
sentences.zh: 你把我的朋友萨姆吃掉了吗？

sentences.en: I chuckled, but in a complicated key.
sentences.zh: 我笑了笑，但笑声中带着复杂的情绪。

sentences.en: Like many Americans, I put on serious weight during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 像许多美国人一样，我在疫情期间胖了很多。

sentences.en: How much?
sentences.zh: 胖了多少？

sentences.en: No idea.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: It had been years since I'd stepped on a scale.
sentences.zh: 我已经好几年没站上体重秤了。

sentences.en: We were suffering a worldwide super trauma.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正遭受着一场全球性的巨大创伤。

sentences.en: And my approach to calamities has always been extremely simple.
sentences.zh: 而我应对灾难的方法一直非常简单。

sentences.en: I snack.
sentences.zh: 我吃零食。

sentences.en: Do you know the saying, don't fill up on chips?
sentences.zh: 你知道那句谚语吗，别吃薯片吃饱了？

sentences.en: That saying is about me.
sentences.zh: 那句话说的就是我。

sentences.en: I am the guy who fills up on chips.
sentences.zh: 我就是那个会用薯片填饱肚子的人。

sentences.en: During the pandemic, I snacked the way other people knit or whittled or shuffled cards.
sentences.zh: 疫情期间，我吃零食的方式就像别人织毛衣、雕刻或洗牌一样。

sentences.en: Anxiously, obsessively, to keep my spirit from hissing out of my ear.
sentences.zh: 焦虑地、强迫性地，为了不让我的灵魂从耳朵里嘶嘶溜走。

sentences.en: I turned myself into my own personal foie gras goose.
sentences.zh: 我把自己变成了一只供自己享用的肥鹅。

sentences.en: Guzzling chips, chocolate, chocolate chips, peanut butter, peanut butter chocolate chips, chocolate peanut butter ice cream sprinkled with peanut butter chocolate chips.
sentences.zh: 狂吃薯片、巧克力、巧克力豆、花生酱、花生酱巧克力豆，还有撒着花生酱巧克力豆的巧克力花生酱冰淇淋。

sentences.en: And so, bulge by bulge, lump by lump, my body grew all the infamous mounds and blobs our culture likes to invent insulting nicknames for.
sentences.zh: 于是，随着一圈圈赘肉的堆积，我的身体长出了所有那些文化喜欢发明侮辱性绰号的部位。

sentences.en: A muffin top, moobs, and most especially, love handles.
sentences.zh: 松饼顶、男乳，尤其是腰间赘肉。

sentences.en: As an inner circle friend, Alan had every right to make that little joke.
sentences.zh: 作为核心圈的朋友，艾伦完全有权开那个小玩笑。

sentences.en: I probably would have said the same to him.
sentences.zh: 我可能也会对他这么说。

sentences.en: Still, it lodged in my mind.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，它还是留在了我的脑海里。

sentences.en: And sometimes, late at night, it clicked on like a broken flashlight.
sentences.zh: 有时在深夜，它就像一把坏掉的手电筒一样突然闪现。

sentences.en: Another bad body moment happened in Cape Cod during a supposedly fun beach vacation when I discovered that none of my shorts would fit.
sentences.zh: 另一个糟糕的身体时刻发生在科德角，那本该是一次愉快的海滩度假，但我发现我所有的短裤都穿不上了。

sentences.en: I had packed many pairs, but all their waistbands were suddenly like wristbands.
sentences.zh: 我带了很多条，但它们的腰围突然间都变得像腕带一样紧。

sentences.en: And so, I had to leave my family and go walking downtown, wearing shorts so tight I couldn't even button them
sentences.zh: 于是，我不得不离开家人，走在市中心，穿着紧到连扣子都扣不上的短裤，

sentences.en: through crowds of sculpted, shirtless Provincetown men showing off their beach bodies.
sentences.zh: 穿过一群群身材健美、赤裸上身、炫耀着海滩身材的普罗温斯敦男人们。

sentences.en: Finally, after a long, sad time in a dressing room, I came out wearing a pair of huge black cut-off jean shorts that I did not even like.
sentences.zh: 最后，在试衣间里度过了一段漫长而悲伤的时光后，我穿着一条我根本不喜欢的大号黑色牛仔短裤走了出来。

sentences.en: But this was when things took a turn.
sentences.zh: 但就在这时，事情出现了转机。

sentences.en: The man at the counter, a slim Cape Cod fashion plate with tanned arms popping out of his tank top, looked me over gravely, lowered his voice, and confided something amazing.
sentences.zh: 柜台后的男人，一个身材苗条、穿着背心露出古铜色手臂的科德角时尚达人，严肃地打量了我一番，压低声音，向我透露了一件惊人的事。

sentences.en: You know, he said, that's exactly where I was six months ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，他说，六个月前我就是这个样子。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I said.
sentences.zh: 我问。

sentences.en: I felt as if I had stepped into a weight loss commercial, and I was unable to stop myself from saying the next line in the script.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己仿佛走进了一则减肥广告，我不由自主地接出了剧本里的下一句台词。

sentences.en: What did you do?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Dude, I'll be honest with you, the shopkeeper said.
sentences.zh: 伙计，我跟你说实话，店主说。

sentences.en: And still, all these months later, I find it touching that he addressed me as dude.
sentences.zh: 直到现在，几个月过去了，我依然觉得他称呼我为“伙计”很感人。

sentences.en: It was, in a vulnerable moment, an unexpected little charge of tender, masculine care.
sentences.zh: 在那脆弱的时刻，那是一种意想不到的、温柔的、充满男性关怀的慰藉。

sentences.en: He hated to admit it, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，他其实不想承认这一点。

sentences.en: But what enabled him to lose all his pandemic weight was a weight loss app.
sentences.zh: 但让他减掉所有疫情期间增加的体重的方法，就是一个减肥软件。

sentences.en: It sucks, he told me.
sentences.zh: 这很烂，他告诉我。

sentences.en: But in his experience, it was the only way.
sentences.zh: 但在他的经验里，这是唯一的方法。

sentences.en: You have to log your meals and count your calories until everything is back under control.
sentences.zh: 你必须记录你的饮食并计算卡路里，直到一切恢复正常。

sentences.en: In the weeks after this conversation, walking around in my black jean shorts, I suffered some more bad moments.
sentences.zh: 在那次谈话后的几周里，穿着黑色牛仔短裤走来走去的我，又经历了一些糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: Until, eventually, with mixed feelings, I broke down and took the Provincetown shopkeeper's advice.
sentences.zh: 直到最后，带着复杂的心情，我妥协了，采纳了那位普罗温斯敦店主的建议。

sentences.en: I poked around on my phone and downloaded a weight loss app called Noom.
sentences.zh: 我在手机上捣鼓了一番，下载了一个叫 Noom 的减肥软件。

sentences.en: It seemed to be suddenly ubiquitous online, popping up in tweets and banner ads, and in a random testimonial from someone I followed on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 它似乎突然在网上无处不在，出现在推文、横幅广告以及我在 Instagram 上关注的人发布的随机推荐中。

sentences.en: I felt silly about it, so at first I didn't tell anyone.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很傻，所以起初我没告诉任何人。

sentences.en: Yes, I found it humiliating to be overweight, but I also found it humiliating to be worried about being overweight.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得超重很丢人，但我也觉得为超重而感到焦虑很丢人。

sentences.en: I wanted to lose the weight, but didn't want to be seen wanting to lose the weight, even by myself.
sentences.zh: 我想减肥，但不想被别人看到我想减肥，甚至不想让自己看到。

sentences.en: You can tell what Noom is like from its name.
sentences.zh: 从名字你就能看出 Noom 是什么样的。

sentences.en: One syllable of cutesy app babble that seems to suggest real language, Noom-me, without actually meaning anything.
sentences.zh: 一个听起来像可爱应用术语的单音节词，似乎暗示着某种真实的语言，Noom-me，但实际上毫无意义。

sentences.en: Noom is to diet culture what a cool youth pastor is to organized religion, a kind of good vibes modulation of something that might otherwise put people off.
sentences.zh: Noom 之于节食文化，就像酷炫的青年牧师之于有组织的宗教，是对某种原本可能让人反感的事物进行的一种“正能量”调节。

sentences.en: The core of Noom's personality is that it is always trying very, very, very hard.
sentences.zh: Noom 个性的核心在于它总是非常、非常、非常努力。

sentences.en: Sometimes my phone will flash and I'll think I have a text or a news alert, but it will just
sentences.zh: 有时我的手机会闪烁，我以为是短信或新闻提醒，但其实只是

sentences.en: be Noom saying something like, we're blinded by your 51st meal in a row glow up, star eyes emoji, or batter up, but hold the batter, winking emoji.
sentences.zh: Noom 在说类似这样的话：我们被你连续第51餐的蜕变闪瞎了眼（星星眼表情），或者准备击球，但别挥棒（眨眼表情）。

sentences.en: It's time to log dinner.
sentences.zh: 该记录晚餐了。

sentences.en: Every morning,
sentences.zh: 每天早上，

sentences.en: Noom gives me little quizzes about nutrition and water intake and caloric density.
sentences.zh: Noom 都会给我出一些关于营养、水分摄入和热量密度的小测验。

sentences.en: And whenever I guess right, it says corny words like Noomalicious, and then rewards me for my achievements
sentences.zh: 每当我猜对时，它就会说一些俗气的词，比如“Noomalicious”，然后用 Noom 硬币奖励我的成就，

sentences.en: with Noom coins that move a piece on a game board as if I were a child playing Candyland.
sentences.zh: 让我像个玩糖果乐园游戏的孩子一样在棋盘上移动棋子。

sentences.en: I am a middle-aged man with a mortgage and teenage children and a beard.
sentences.zh: 我是一个有房贷、有十几岁孩子、留着胡子的中年男人。

sentences.en: I have arthritis in my ankles.
sentences.zh: 我的脚踝有关节炎。

sentences.en: Please excuse me for a moment while I schedule my next colonoscopy.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我一会儿，我要去预约下一次肠镜检查了。

sentences.en: Do I really need to spend a large part of every day being treated like a preschooler with a sticker chart?
sentences.zh: 我真的需要每天花大量时间被当作一个拿着贴纸奖励表的学龄前儿童来对待吗？

sentences.en: Well, humiliatingly, yes I do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，虽然很丢人，但我确实需要。

sentences.en: I seem to need this very badly.
sentences.zh: 我似乎非常需要这个。

sentences.en: Because the psychological hardware that governs my in-the-moment relationship to food is apparently five years old.
sentences.zh: 因为支配我当下饮食关系的心理硬件显然只有五岁大。

sentences.en: In fact, this might be why Noom worked for me.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可能就是 Noom 对我有效的原因。

sentences.en: Not despite its annoying, cutesy tone, but because of it.
sentences.zh: 不是尽管它那恼人、可爱的语气，而是正因为如此。

sentences.en: That candy-colored, cartoonish frequency allowed it to reach the tiny child in me.
sentences.zh: 那种糖果色、卡通化的频率让它能够触及我内心那个小孩子。

sentences.en: The tiny, chubby child who first struggled with his weight.
sentences.zh: 那个最早开始为体重而挣扎的、胖乎乎的小孩。

sentences.en: Almost right away, the app got me to do two simple things that turned out to be radical acts.
sentences.zh: 几乎立刻，这个软件就让我做了两件简单的事情，结果证明这是激进的举动。

sentences.en: To weigh in every morning, and to track everything I put in my mouth.
sentences.zh: 每天早上称重，并记录我吃进嘴里的每一件东西。

sentences.en: That was basically the whole program.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是整个计划的全部。

sentences.en: Pay attention to what you eat, make conscious decisions,
sentences.zh: 注意你吃的东西，做出有意识的决定，

sentences.en: stick to a rough calorie budget, note your progress, and keep doing all that until the good behavior becomes habitual.
sentences.zh: 坚持一个粗略的卡路里预算，记录你的进展，并一直这样做，直到良好的行为成为习惯。

sentences.en: I didn't want to enter fifty handfuls of gorp into my food log, so I would leave the lid on the gorp tub, and, if I actually felt hungry, not just bored or worried, I would eat
sentences.zh: 我不想在食物记录里输入五十把混合坚果，所以我干脆把坚果罐的盖子盖上，如果我真的感到饿了，而不是仅仅感到无聊或焦虑，我就吃

sentences.en: an apple instead.
sentences.zh: 一个苹果代替。

sentences.en: Wait, are you calorie restricting?
sentences.zh: 等等，你在限制卡路里吗？

sentences.en: My wife asked me one morning as she watched me counting almonds.
sentences.zh: 我妻子有一天早上看着我数杏仁时问我。

sentences.en: Hold on, my teenage daughter said.
sentences.zh: 等等，我十几岁的女儿说。

sentences.en: Are you logging everything you eat and weighing yourself every day?
sentences.zh: 你在记录你吃的所有东西，而且每天都在称重？

sentences.en: I don't like that.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: I admitted that, yes, I was doing those things, and that I didn't particularly like it either.
sentences.zh: 我承认，是的，我确实在做这些事，而且我也不太喜欢这样。

sentences.en: It was not my first or second or hundredth choice.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的第一、第二或第一百个选择。

sentences.en: But I disliked the alternative more.
sentences.zh: 但我更不喜欢另一种选择。

sentences.en: Eating when I wasn't hungry, eating until I felt almost sick, mindlessly inhaling
sentences.zh: 在不饿的时候进食，吃到几乎想吐，毫无意识地吞下

sentences.en: whatever heaps of processed food the multinational snack conglomerates managed to stick in front of my face all day long.
sentences.zh: 跨国零食集团整天塞到我面前的任何加工食品堆。

sentences.en: And I had no idea how to break those deep habits on my own.
sentences.zh: 而且我不知道如何靠自己打破这些根深蒂固的习惯。

sentences.en: There seemed to be dangers on all sides.
sentences.zh: 危险似乎四面八方都有。

sentences.en: I didn't want to inject myself with the well-documented toxicity of diet culture, obsessive restriction.
sentences.zh: 我不想给自己注入节食文化中那种有据可查的毒性，那种强迫性的限制。

sentences.en: But I also didn't want to abandon myself to out-of-control excess.
sentences.zh: 但我也不想让自己陷入失控的放纵中。

sentences.en: It seemed like a very small needle to thread.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个非常难穿过的针眼。

sentences.en: For whatever reason, shockingly, depressingly, triumphantly, problematically, Noom worked.
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因，令人震惊、令人沮丧、令人欣喜、令人困惑的是，Noom 奏效了。

sentences.en: In my first week, I lost three and a half pounds.
sentences.zh: 第一周，我瘦了三点五磅。

sentences.en: Within two weeks, I'd lost seven.
sentences.zh: 两周内，我瘦了七磅。

sentences.en: Within a couple of months, I had lost all my pandemic weight and more.
sentences.zh: 几个月内，我减掉了所有疫情期间增加的体重，甚至更多。

sentences.en: And the weight kept coming off.
sentences.zh: 而且体重还在持续下降。

sentences.en: Enough to unlock vast wardrobes of old clothing.
sentences.zh: 足以解锁我衣柜里大量旧衣服。

sentences.en: Pants I hadn't worn in years.
sentences.zh: 我好几年没穿过的裤子。

sentences.en: Favorite t-shirts I'd given to my daughter.
sentences.zh: 我送给女儿的最爱T恤。

sentences.en: My wife asked if I maybe secretly had cancer.
sentences.zh: 我妻子问我是不是偷偷得了癌症。

sentences.en: But I didn't, as far as anyone could tell.
sentences.zh: 但据大家所知，我并没有。

sentences.en: All of that weight was just from snacking, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，所有这些体重只是因为吃零食。

sentences.en: All these years, all you needed to do was pay attention.
sentences.zh: 这么多年来，你所需要做的只是多加注意。

sentences.en: Suddenly, I was slim.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我变瘦了。

sentences.en: It was, by any measure, an incredible weight loss success story.
sentences.zh: 无论从什么标准来看，这都是一个令人难以置信的减肥成功故事。

sentences.en: Even my great friend Alan texted me about how good I looked.
sentences.zh: 连我的挚友艾伦都发短信说我看起来状态很好。

sentences.en: Did I say that, he wrote, with a face palm emoji, when I reminded him of the time he squeezed my love handles?
sentences.zh: 我当时真的那么说了吗？他写道，并配上了一个扶额的表情，当我提醒他那次他捏我腰间赘肉的时候。

sentences.en: Sam, I was very inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 萨姆，我当时太不礼貌了。

sentences.en: But I still think it's funny.
sentences.zh: 但我还是觉得这很好笑。

sentences.en: I had achieved the great transformation.
sentences.zh: 我已经完成了那场伟大的蜕变。

sentences.en: I had turned myself into the after photo.
sentences.zh: 我把自己变成了那张“之后”的照片。

sentences.en: And now that we have that out of the way, I can tell you what I consider the most interesting thing about my weight loss journey.
sentences.zh: 既然已经把这个说完了，我可以告诉你，我认为我减肥历程中最有趣的事情是什么。

sentences.en: A secret that you will never see in any banner ad.
sentences.zh: 一个你在任何横幅广告里都永远看不到的秘密。

sentences.en: As the months passed, as I stuck with my healthful habits, and got used to my new trim body, as the line on my noom weight graph stayed low,
sentences.zh: 随着几个月过去，我坚持着健康的生活习惯，习惯了我那修长的新身材，随着Noom体重图表上的曲线保持在低位，

sentences.en: I felt something amazing.
sentences.zh: 我感受到了一种奇妙的感觉。

sentences.en: I felt pretty much exactly as I had always felt my whole entire life.
sentences.zh: 我感觉和我这一生中一直以来的感觉几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: I was, after all that change, still only myself.
sentences.zh: 经历了所有这些改变后，我依然只是我自己。

sentences.en: My big epiphany, if I could put it into words, would be something like, so what?
sentences.zh: 如果非要用语言来表达，我最大的顿悟大概就是：那又怎样？

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: What is the human relationship to the body?
sentences.zh: 人类与身体的关系是什么？

sentences.en: Is it like a roommate?
sentences.zh: 就像室友吗？

sentences.en: A pet?
sentences.zh: 宠物？

sentences.en: A twin?
sentences.zh: 双胞胎？

sentences.en: A teammate?
sentences.zh: 队友？

sentences.en: A rival?
sentences.zh: 对手？

sentences.en: A parasite?
sentences.zh: 寄生虫？

sentences.en: A host?
sentences.zh: 宿主？

sentences.en: Is the body our essential self?
sentences.zh: 身体是我们本质的自我吗？

sentences.en: Or is it just an outer shell?
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅是一个外壳？

sentences.en: And if so, is it more like a clam shell?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，它更像是一个蛤蜊壳吗？

sentences.en: Homegrown, enduring?
sentences.zh: 原生、持久？

sentences.en: Or a hermit crab shell?
sentences.zh: 还是寄居蟹的壳？

sentences.en: Adopted?
sentences.zh: 领养的？

sentences.en: Adopted?
sentences.zh: 领养的？

sentences.en: Temporary?
sentences.zh: 暂时的？

sentences.en: Is it closer to a tamale husk?
sentences.zh: 它更接近玉米粽的叶子吗？

sentences.en: Or a hot dog bun?
sentences.zh: 还是热狗面包？

sentences.en: Or a pita pocket?
sentences.zh: 或者是皮塔饼口袋？

sentences.en: Or the fluorescent cake tube that wraps a Twinkies sweet cream center?
sentences.zh: 又或者是包裹着Twinkies奶油夹心的荧光色蛋糕管？

sentences.en: Is the body the other side of the coin of the mind?
sentences.zh: 身体是心灵这枚硬币的另一面吗？

sentences.en: Or is the body the whole coin itself?
sentences.zh: 还是说身体本身就是整枚硬币？

sentences.en: And the mind is just the series of images and slogans stamped superficially on the exterior.
sentences.zh: 而心灵只是那些肤浅地印在表面的图像和口号？

sentences.en: Is the body an ancient piece of hardware designed to run the cutting-edge software of our souls?
sentences.zh: 身体是一台古老的硬件，旨在运行我们灵魂那尖端的软件吗？

sentences.en: Or is it more like a hostage situation?
sentences.zh: 还是更像一场人质劫持事件？

sentences.en: Is the body a time bomb strapped to our existence?
sentences.zh: 身体是绑在我们生命上的一枚定时炸弹吗？

sentences.en: The thing that will bring the action movie of our life to a sudden, unpredictable end?
sentences.zh: 那个会将我们人生的动作大片带向突然、不可预测结局的东西？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: None of us do.
sentences.zh: 我们谁都不知道。

sentences.en: This is one of the gnawing weirdnesses of being human.
sentences.zh: 这是身为人类令人抓狂的怪事之一。

sentences.en: It is impossible to think your body.
sentences.zh: 你不可能通过思考来理解你的身体。

sentences.en: You can only really body your body.
sentences.zh: 你真正能做的只有去“体验”你的身体。

sentences.en: And so we walk around with this feeling of mild alienation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们带着这种轻微的疏离感四处走动。

sentences.en: This basic incoherence.
sentences.zh: 这种基本的脱节感。

sentences.en: A dualism that runs all the way to the roots of Western culture.
sentences.zh: 一种贯穿西方文化根源的二元论。

sentences.en: You can find it in Plato, who said, If we would have true knowledge of anything, we must be quit of the body.
sentences.zh: 你可以在柏拉图那里找到它，他说：“如果我们想对任何事物有真正的认识，我们就必须摆脱身体。”

sentences.en: And in the Bible, which says, What?
sentences.zh: 还有《圣经》里说，什么？

sentences.en: Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost, which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
sentences.zh: “岂不知你们的身子就是圣灵的殿吗？这圣灵是从神而来，住在你们里头的；并且你们不是自己的人。”

sentences.en: Or, to quote the comedian John Mulaney, I don't know what my body is for, other than just taking my head from room to room.
sentences.zh: 或者，引用喜剧演员约翰·穆兰尼的话：“除了把我的头从一个房间带到另一个房间，我不知道我的身体有什么用。”

sentences.en: What I know about my body, for sure, is its size.
sentences.zh: 关于我的身体，我唯一确定知道的就是它的尺寸。

sentences.en: When it is bigger or smaller, squishier or firmer.
sentences.zh: 当它变大或变小，变软或变硬的时候。

sentences.en: I know this every day, firsthand, from point-blank range.
sentences.zh: 我每天都能亲身感受到，近距离地观察到。

sentences.en: I should acknowledge here that I've been lucky.
sentences.zh: 我应该在这里承认，我很幸运。

sentences.en: I've never struggled with an eating disorder.
sentences.zh: 我从未受过饮食失调的困扰。

sentences.en: Have never been grievously hurt by diet culture.
sentences.zh: 也从未被节食文化严重伤害过。

sentences.en: Noom, by the way, tries to position itself as above diet culture.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，Noom试图将自己定位在节食文化之上。

sentences.en: But it absolutely is not, as many critics have pointed out.
sentences.zh: 但正如许多批评家指出的那样，它绝对不是。

sentences.en: Even so, my weight has somehow managed to make itself a central fact of my life, an essential part of the story I tell myself about myself.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我的体重还是设法成为了我生活中的一个核心事实，成为我对自己讲述的故事中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: In our number-obsessed culture, people tend to use weight as diagnostic shorthand for the whole vexed mind-body relationship.
sentences.zh: 在我们这个痴迷于数字的文化中，人们倾向于将体重作为一种诊断速记，来概括整个令人困扰的身心关系。

sentences.en: It serves as a kind of stock price, a number that indicates publicly the overall health of our private situations.
sentences.zh: 它就像一种股票价格，一个公开显示我们私人生活整体健康状况的数字。

sentences.en: For much of my childhood, I was the fat kid.
sentences.zh: 在我童年的大部分时间里，我都是那个胖孩子。

sentences.en: Husky was a word I heard a lot.
sentences.zh: “壮实”是我常听到的一个词。

sentences.en: As a chubby child, I remember staring at photos of my mother as a chubby child.
sentences.zh: 作为一个胖乎乎的孩子，我记得我盯着我母亲小时候胖乎乎的照片看。

sentences.en: Her big, round cheeks were my big, round cheeks.
sentences.zh: 她那圆圆的大脸颊就是我那圆圆的大脸颊。

sentences.en: We looked as if we were both peeking out, shyly, over a pair of ripe mangoes.
sentences.zh: 我们看起来就像是害羞地从一对熟透的芒果后面探出头来。

sentences.en: This was both a comfort and a curse.
sentences.zh: 这既是一种安慰，也是一种诅咒。

sentences.en: To see my own face reflected across the decades.
sentences.zh: 看到我自己的脸在几十年间映照出来。

sentences.en: To know that my mom had been there firSt. To recognize my body as an intergenerational mirror.
sentences.zh: 知道我妈妈也曾经历过这一切。意识到我的身体是一面跨越代际的镜子。

sentences.en: I understood that I was just a sequence of genes, activated and expanding, filling in the generous outlines of my ancestors.
sentences.zh: 我明白我只是一连串基因的序列，被激活并扩张，填补了我祖先那宽厚的轮廓。

sentences.en: As a kid with a big, soft body, I suffered all the usual troubles.
sentences.zh: 作为一个有着大而柔软身体的孩子，我遭受了所有常见的烦恼。

sentences.en: I was the slowest possible runner.
sentences.zh: 我是跑得最慢的人。

sentences.en: I dreaded taking my shirt off at public pools.
sentences.zh: 我害怕在公共游泳池脱掉衬衫。

sentences.en: Sometimes other kids laughed at me.
sentences.zh: 有时其他孩子会嘲笑我。

sentences.en: I felt like a loser because I feared that the largeness of my body would relegate me to a sad small corner of the culture.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己是个失败者，因为我担心我身体的肥胖会把我放逐到文化中一个悲伤的小角落。

sentences.en: Movies and TV were clear on this point.
sentences.zh: 电影和电视在这一点上很明确。

sentences.en: The fat kid could be a funny sidekick, but not the main character.
sentences.zh: 胖孩子可以是搞笑的配角，但不能是主角。

sentences.en: The best he could hope for was, at some point, to transform.
sentences.zh: 他能期待的最好的结果，就是在某个时刻发生蜕变。

sentences.en: To find a way to shed the extra weight and unleash his essential self.
sentences.zh: 找到一种方法减掉多余的体重，释放出他本质的自我。

sentences.en: My mom had it harder.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈经历的更艰难。

sentences.en: Her father was a tough guy, a slim cattle rancher, who galloped through life, correcting everything that struck him as wrong.
sentences.zh: 她父亲是个硬汉，一个瘦削的牧牛人，他风风火火地过了一生，纠正着一切他认为错误的事情。

sentences.en: Many things struck him as wrong.
sentences.zh: 很多事情在他看来都是错的。

sentences.en: Once, infamously, he watched me drink a whole glass of apple juice, and then told me, very seriously, that I had done it improperly.
sentences.zh: 有一次，臭名昭著的是，他看着我喝完一整杯苹果汁，然后非常严肃地告诉我，我喝得不对。

sentences.en: You drank it for the flavor, he said, not the nutrition.
sentences.zh: 他说，你是为了味道而喝，而不是为了营养。

sentences.en: That is a ridiculous thing to say, obviously, but I should also admit that he was correct.
sentences.zh: 这显然是很荒谬的说法，但我也得承认他是对的。

sentences.en: I was absolutely drinking that juice for the flavor.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是为了味道才喝那杯果汁的。

sentences.en: I was surrendering myself completely, unreasonably, unreasonably, to the pleasure of consumption.
sentences.zh: 我完全、不合理地、不合理地沉溺于消费的快感中。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: This is the great subversive joy of a snack.
sentences.zh: 这就是零食带来的巨大颠覆性快乐。

sentences.en: It is meaningless eating.
sentences.zh: 那是毫无意义的进食。

sentences.en: Eating purely for eating's sake.
sentences.zh: 纯粹为了吃而吃。

sentences.en: Eating detached from nutrition, and even, in the end, from appetite itself.
sentences.zh: 脱离了营养，甚至最终脱离了食欲本身的进食。

sentences.en: I was, back then, a legendary snacker.
sentences.zh: 那时候，我是一个传奇的零食爱好者。

sentences.en: A little monster of appetite.
sentences.zh: 一个小小的食欲怪兽。

sentences.en: In the school cafeteria, I was famous, several tables over, for stuffing my mouth with brownies.
sentences.zh: 在学校食堂里，我很有名，隔着好几张桌子，大家都知道我往嘴里塞布朗尼蛋糕。

sentences.en: It was a whole high-wire act.
sentences.zh: 那简直是一场高空走钢丝表演。

sentences.en: Kids would donate their desserts, and watch them disappear all at once into my face.
sentences.zh: 孩子们会捐出他们的甜点，看着它们一下子全部消失在我的嘴里。

sentences.en: And my cheeks would swell, hamster-style, until I could barely breathe.
sentences.zh: 我的脸颊会像仓鼠一样鼓起来，直到我几乎无法呼吸。

sentences.en: And everyone would point and laugh while I chewed and swallowed for many minutes.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会指着我大笑，而我则咀嚼并吞咽了好几分钟。

sentences.en: I loved the attention, of course, but my deeper motivation was really just that I wanted to eat all those brownies.
sentences.zh: 我当然喜欢这种关注，但我更深层的动机其实只是因为我想吃掉所有那些布朗尼。

sentences.en: And crucially, I wanted to eat them all at once.
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要的是，我想一次性把它们全吃掉。

sentences.en: I remember thinking about these issues, philosophically, in the mornings as I walked to school.
sentences.zh: 我记得每天早上走去学校时，都会从哲学角度思考这些问题。

sentences.en: When faced with the last half of a
sentences.zh: 当面对最后半块

sentences.en: Snickers bar, I mused, was it better to eat it in multiple bites, moderately, savoring each morsel, drawing out the pleasure?
sentences.zh: 士力架时，我思忖着，是分多次适度地吃掉它，细细品味每一口，延长快乐更好？

sentences.en: Or was it better, theoretically speaking, to inhale the whole thing in one gooey, choking mouthful?
sentences.zh: 还是从理论上讲，一口气把它吸进嘴里，那种黏糊糊、噎人的感觉更好？

sentences.en: Cheeks heaving, batching every remaining flavor molecule into a giant extinction burst, a moment of total sensory overload?
sentences.zh: 脸颊起伏，将每一个残留的味道分子汇聚成一次巨大的爆发，一种感官完全超载的时刻？

sentences.en: I decided firmly, without question, that my soul was a one-bite soul.
sentences.zh: 我坚定地决定，毫无疑问，我的灵魂是一个“一口吞”的灵魂。

sentences.en: Still, I did not like being fat.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我还是不喜欢变胖。

sentences.en: Throughout my childhood, as I watched my mother gain and lose weight, as I tagged along to her weight loss meetings and
sentences.zh: 整个童年时期，看着我母亲增重又减重，跟着她去参加减肥会议和

sentences.en: jazzercise classes, I became fluent in the slogans of 1980s diet culture.
sentences.zh: 爵士健美操课，我变得对80年代节食文化的口号非常熟悉。

sentences.en: No pain, no gain.
sentences.zh: 没有痛苦，就没有收获。

sentences.en: A moment on the lips, a lifetime on the hips.
sentences.zh: 嘴上一时爽，臀上一生债。

sentences.en: Inside every fat person, there is a skinny person waiting to get out.
sentences.zh: 每个胖子内心都住着一个等待破茧而出的瘦子。

sentences.en: I remember standing in the shower in sixth grade, feeling disgusted by my body, grabbing a handful of my floppy belly, and saying to myself, this is not who I really am.
sentences.zh: 我记得六年级时站在淋浴间里，对自己身体感到厌恶，抓起一把松垮的肚皮，对自己说：这不是真正的我。

sentences.en: I was reciting unconsciously the cultural script.
sentences.zh: 我是在无意识地背诵文化剧本。

sentences.en: And so, at 12, I summoned my willpower and started jogging.
sentences.zh: 于是，12岁那年，我鼓起意志力开始慢跑。

sentences.en: By the end of middle school, I was fairly slim.
sentences.zh: 到初中结束时，我已经相当苗条了。

sentences.en: By high school, I was a decent athlete.
sentences.zh: 到了高中，我成了一个不错的运动员。

sentences.en: In retrospect, I think what really slimmed me down were hormones and growth spurts.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，我认为真正让我瘦下来的是荷尔蒙和生长发育。

sentences.en: But that achievement became a pillar of my teenage identity, a story I loved to tell about myself.
sentences.zh: 但那种成就感成了我青少年身份的支柱，一个我喜欢讲述的关于我自己的故事。

sentences.en: I had been a fat kid, a kid living under a genetic curse.
sentences.zh: 我曾经是个胖孩子，一个生活在基因诅咒下的孩子。

sentences.en: But then, through the miracle of willpower and self-discipline, I overcame.
sentences.zh: 但后来，通过意志力和自律的奇迹，我克服了。

sentences.en: Or did I actually overcome?
sentences.zh: 或者说，我真的克服了吗？

sentences.en: What diet stories tend to leave out is that, in the wake of restriction, people almost always gain the weight back.
sentences.zh: 节食故事往往忽略的一点是，在节食之后，人们几乎总是会反弹。

sentences.en: The story of a life is much longer than the story of a diet.
sentences.zh: 人生的故事远比节食的故事长得多。

sentences.en: Over the decades, my weight has fluctuated widely, as I have pinged between poles of excess and restriction, appetite and control, abstinence and snacking.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，我的体重波动很大，我在过度与节制、食欲与控制、禁欲与零食的两极之间来回摇摆。

sentences.en: Or, as my grandfather might put it, flavor and nutrition.
sentences.zh: 或者，用我祖父的话说，味道与营养。

sentences.en: I have an alter ego that my wife calls, with affectionate amazement,
sentences.zh: 我有一个“另一个自我”，我妻子带着深情的惊叹称之为

sentences.en: Fat Sam.
sentences.zh: “胖山姆”。

sentences.en: She first met him on our honeymoon.
sentences.zh: 她第一次见到他是在我们的蜜月期间。

sentences.en: We'd been driving all day, rolling through the high desert near Santa Fe, watching huge thunderstorms flickering over black mesas, trying to get to where we were going.
sentences.zh: 我们开车开了一整天，穿过圣达菲附近的高地沙漠，看着巨大的雷暴在黑色平顶山上闪烁，试图赶往目的地。

sentences.en: And when we finally did, in the middle of the night, famished and exhausted, the only open restaurant was Denny's.
sentences.zh: 当我们终于在半夜到达时，饥肠辘辘且精疲力竭，唯一开着的餐厅是丹尼餐厅。

sentences.en: And the only thing on my mind was merging, body and soul, with the first cheeseburger that passed by.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里想的唯一一件事，就是身心合一地与第一个经过的芝士汉堡融为一体。

sentences.en: The moment my meal arrived, the universe seemed to crack in half, like an eggshell in the hands of a line cook.
sentences.zh: 当我餐点送达的那一刻，宇宙似乎裂成了两半，就像厨师手中的蛋壳一样。

sentences.en: And a brand new character crawled out, Fat Sam.
sentences.zh: 一个全新的角色爬了出来，胖山姆。

sentences.en: Fat Sam attacked the food in front of him with wild urgency.
sentences.zh: 胖山姆以狂野的急迫感攻击着面前的食物。

sentences.en: As I ate, my wife kept trying to say something, to start a conversation.
sentences.zh: 当我吃的时候，我妻子一直试图说些什么，想开启一段对话。

sentences.en: But I would be in the middle of chewing, or near the end of chewing, or just at the beginning of chewing.
sentences.zh: 但我要么正处于咀嚼中，要么快咀嚼完，要么刚开始咀嚼。

sentences.en: And I would hold up one finger, as if to say, yes, hang on just a second, I have an answer for you.
sentences.zh: 我会竖起一根手指，仿佛在说：是的，等一下，我有个答案要告诉你。

sentences.en: But then, in the moment of swallowing, when my mouth was briefly clear, when I could have spoken, I would immediately shove the cheeseburger
sentences.zh: 但随后，在吞咽的那一刻，当我的嘴巴短暂清空，本可以说话的时候，我会立即把芝士汉堡

sentences.en: back into my mouth and take another bite.
sentences.zh: 塞回嘴里，再咬一口。

sentences.en: I was in a kind of trance.
sentences.zh: 我进入了一种恍惚状态。

sentences.en: I was like a horn player doing circular breathing.
sentences.zh: 我就像一个在练习循环呼吸的管乐手。

sentences.en: At one point, the waitress came over and said, how is everything?
sentences.zh: 有一次，女服务员走过来问：一切都好吗？

sentences.en: And with my mouth absolutely overflowing, sounding like a drunken man, moaning with almost sexual ecstasy, I shouted, oh, it's really, really good.
sentences.zh: 我嘴里塞得满满当当，声音听起来像个醉汉，带着近乎性高潮般的呻吟，喊道：哦，真的，真的太好吃了。

sentences.en: And everyone in the room realized at the same time that she had not even been talking to us, but to the table behind us.
sentences.zh: 房间里的每个人同时意识到，她根本不是在和我们说话，而是在和我们身后的那张桌子说话。

sentences.en: Fat Sam didn't care.
sentences.zh: 胖山姆才不在乎。

sentences.en: He just kept cramming the universe into his face.
sentences.zh: 他只是不停地把整个世界塞进嘴里。

sentences.en: The classic diet slogan that made such an impression on me as a chubby child, inside every fat person, there's a skinny person waiting to get out, should, in my case, be reversed.
sentences.zh: 那个在我童年胖乎乎时给我留下深刻印象的经典减肥口号——每个胖子身体里都住着一个想出来的瘦子——在我身上应该反过来才对。

sentences.en: No matter what my body happens to look like, at any particular moment, Fat Sam lives inside me.
sentences.zh: 无论我的身体在任何特定时刻看起来是什么样，胖山姆都住在我心里。

sentences.en: I recognize now, in fact, that Fat Sam represents some of my best qualities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我现在认识到，胖山姆代表了我身上一些最好的品质。

sentences.en: Curiosity, cheerful appetite, a hunger for life, satisfaction in the moment.
sentences.zh: 好奇心、愉快的食欲、对生活的热望，以及对当下的满足感。

sentences.en: Fat Sam's mission is to consume the world in giant gulps of joy.
sentences.zh: 胖山姆的使命就是大口大口地吞咽世界的快乐。

sentences.en: It doesn't even have to be food.
sentences.zh: 甚至不一定是食物。

sentences.en: It can be naps, or video games, or telling jokes at a party, or walking, or shooting free throws, or reading, or petting a dog.
sentences.zh: 可以是小睡、玩电子游戏、在聚会上讲笑话、散步、投篮、阅读，或者抚摸一只狗。

sentences.en: Whatever satisfies a need, whatever I am starving for.
sentences.zh: 任何能满足需求的东西，任何我所渴望的东西。

sentences.en: And in that transfer, in that passage from outside to inside, in that radical taking in, there is a validation of existence, a proof of being, that I refuse to reject.
sentences.zh: 而在那种转化中，在那种从外到内的过程里，在那种彻底的接纳中，存在着一种对生存的确认，一种对存在的证明，我拒绝否定它。

sentences.en: Fat Sam, in many ways, is precious and good.
sentences.zh: 胖山姆在许多方面都是珍贵而美好的。

sentences.en: He is a funnel into which the universe pours, the pinch in the hourglass.
sentences.zh: 他是宇宙倾泻而入的漏斗，是沙漏中最细的那一点。

sentences.en: He reminds me that all of life is, in a sense, appetite.
sentences.zh: 他提醒我，从某种意义上说，生命就是食欲。

sentences.en: When I choose to deny myself something, it is Fat Sam who is feeding, greedily, on that denial.
sentences.zh: 当我选择拒绝自己某些东西时，正是胖山姆在贪婪地以这种拒绝为食。

sentences.en: One of my favorite photos is a selfie I took, ten days after my father died.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的照片之一是我在父亲去世十天后拍的一张自拍。

sentences.en: It holds a strange paradoxical energy.
sentences.zh: 它蕴含着一种奇怪的矛盾能量。

sentences.en: Mourning and joy.
sentences.zh: 哀伤与喜悦。

sentences.en: Comedy and sorrow.
sentences.zh: 喜剧与悲剧。

sentences.en: Ending and continuing.
sentences.zh: 终结与延续。

sentences.en: I took it in the guest bathroom at my father's house.
sentences.zh: 我是在父亲家的客用浴室里拍的。

sentences.en: When, going through his old things, we discovered a treasure trove of vintage jogging shirts.
sentences.zh: 当时我们正在整理他的旧物，发现了一堆复古慢跑衫的宝藏。

sentences.en: My dad was an avid runner.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸是个狂热的跑步者。

sentences.en: He moved to the jogging hotbed, Eugene, Oregon, during its golden age in the 1970s, when the local shoe company, Nike, was rising, and the legend Steve Prefontaine was
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪70年代的黄金时期搬到了慢跑圣地俄勒冈州尤金市，当时当地的鞋业公司耐克正在崛起，传奇人物史蒂夫·普雷方丹（Steve Prefontaine）正

sentences.en: out running the streets with his famous mustache.
sentences.zh: 留着他那标志性的胡子在街上奔跑。

sentences.en: My father had a mustache like Pre's, and he ran on those same streets.
sentences.zh: 我父亲留着像普雷那样的胡子，也在同样的街道上奔跑。

sentences.en: Year by year, he amassed a huge collection of t-shirts from Eugene's annual race, the Butte to Butte.
sentences.zh: 年复一年，他收集了大量尤金年度赛事“Butte to Butte”的T恤。

sentences.en: Looking through them felt like time travel.
sentences.zh: 翻看这些衣服感觉就像在进行时间旅行。

sentences.en: Wild colors, outdated designs, fonts morphing to keep up with the styles of various decades.
sentences.zh: 狂野的色彩、过时的设计、为了跟上不同年代风格而不断变化的字体。

sentences.en: The shirt I loved most was from 1982.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是1982年的那件。

sentences.en: My father would have run this race when I was four, in preschool, still learning to tie my shoes, just forming my first permanent memories.
sentences.zh: 我父亲参加那场比赛时，我才四岁，还在上幼儿园，还在学系鞋带，刚刚形成最初的永久记忆。

sentences.en: Nearly 40 years later, I held this t-shirt and thought of my dad wearing it, still in his 20s, running up and down the Oregon hills, passing through the raggedy
sentences.zh: 近40年后，我拿着这件T恤，想象着我爸爸穿着它，那时他才20多岁，在俄勒冈的山丘上奔跑，穿过道格拉斯冷杉那斑驳的

sentences.en: shade of Douglas fir trees.
sentences.zh: 树荫。

sentences.en: It was yellow and green, my favorite color scheme, a funky 1970s moss mustard.
sentences.zh: 它是黄绿色的，是我最喜欢的配色，一种时髦的70年代苔藓芥末色。

sentences.en: I could not resist trying it on.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住试穿了一下。

sentences.en: The tag said medium, a size I could sometimes get away with wearing.
sentences.zh: 标签上写着中号，这是我有时还能穿进去的尺码。

sentences.en: But not, it turned out, this medium.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这件中号不行。

sentences.en: Not my father's 1982 medium running shirt.
sentences.zh: 不是我父亲那件1982年的中号跑步衫。

sentences.en: The shirt gave hilariously powerful evidence of something I already knew, that my father's body and my body were two very different things.
sentences.zh: 这件衬衫有力地证明了我早已知道的事实：我父亲的身体和我的身体是截然不同的。

sentences.en: His vintage shirt was comically small, designed for a running junkie with single digit body fat.
sentences.zh: 他那件复古衬衫小得滑稽，是为体脂率个位数的跑步狂人设计的。

sentences.en: And on me, it looked like a water balloon stuffed with potatoes.
sentences.zh: 穿在我身上，看起来就像一个塞满了土豆的水气球。

sentences.en: What struck me as really funny was that I was not even at the time in bad shape, sort of B-minus territory by my standards.
sentences.zh: 让我觉得特别好笑的是，当时我的状态其实并不算太差，按我的标准来看，算是B减水平。

sentences.en: So this sudden, lumpy palimpsest, the absence of my dad's body, the presence of mine, hit me in that
sentences.zh: 所以这种突如其来的、臃肿的重叠感，父亲身体的缺席，我身体的在场，在那一刻

sentences.en: moment as outrageous and weird and sad and embarrassing and funny, all of which I think you can read on my face in the photo.
sentences.zh: 冲击着我，既离谱又怪异，既悲伤又尴尬，还带着好笑，我想你在照片里我的脸上都能读出来。

sentences.en: I imagined my father laughing at me, affectionately, at his big, goofy adult son.
sentences.zh: 我想象着父亲在嘲笑我，带着爱意，看着他那又大又笨拙的成年儿子。

sentences.en: And I then imagined his laughter fading into a shy smile, as it always did.
sentences.zh: 然后我想象他的笑声渐渐变成了一个羞涩的微笑，就像他平时那样。

sentences.en: I imagined him remembering
sentences.zh: 我想象他回想起

sentences.en: 1982, when that shirt would have been bright and new, when his son's body would have been much too small to fill it.
sentences.zh: 1982年，那时这件衬衫还是崭新的，那时他儿子的身体还太小，根本撑不起它。

sentences.en: I had been thinking in those days, a lot about bodies.
sentences.zh: 那几天我一直在思考身体的问题。

sentences.en: At the end of his life, my father was very ill.
sentences.zh: 在生命的最后，我父亲病得很重。

sentences.en: I thought about the way my able body had allowed me to help his suddenly disabled body with its basic functions, just as he helped me with those same functions 40 years before.
sentences.zh: 我想到我健康的身体是如何让我能够帮助他那突然失去功能的身体处理基本生理需求的，就像40年前他帮助我一样。

sentences.en: He could hardly swallow in the end.
sentences.zh: 最后他几乎无法吞咽。

sentences.en: And he had been so skinny.
sentences.zh: 他当时瘦得皮包骨头。

sentences.en: And I felt so close to him.
sentences.zh: 我感到和他如此亲近。

sentences.en: Life can be so sad.
sentences.zh: 生活有时真的很悲伤。

sentences.en: I thought a lot, of course, about the terrible fact that my father's body was now in the ground,
sentences.zh: 当然，我思考了很多关于父亲的身体如今已入土的残酷事实，

sentences.en: that his body was an object, and that my body too would someday be only an object.
sentences.zh: 他的身体变成了一个物体，而我的身体终有一天也会仅仅成为一个物体。

sentences.en: The crisis of my father's body made me think in a new way about the basic crisis of every human body.
sentences.zh: 父亲身体的危机让我以一种新的方式思考每个人身体的基本危机。

sentences.en: That we will always, in the end, be disabled, lose control.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们最终总会失去功能，失去控制。

sentences.en: In many ways, this is what our bodies are.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这就是我们的身体。

sentences.en: Ever-present reminders of our essential lack of control.
sentences.zh: 时刻提醒着我们本质上缺乏控制力。

sentences.en: The body subjects us to gravity and pain.
sentences.zh: 身体让我们受制于重力和疼痛。

sentences.en: It makes us eat, sleep, fall, sit.
sentences.zh: 它让我们吃、睡、跌倒、坐下。

sentences.en: It is the only part of us that can be bitten by a dog or go tumbling down a flight of stairs.
sentences.zh: 它是我们身上唯一会被狗咬伤或从楼梯上滚落的部分。

sentences.en: Much of diet culture is a sublimated response to this crisis.
sentences.zh: 大部分减肥文化是对这种危机的一种升华反应。

sentences.en: An attempt to discipline the unruliness of the body, to transcend it, to prove that we are not, in the end, merely things.
sentences.zh: 试图管教身体的叛逆，超越它，证明我们最终不仅仅是物体。

sentences.en: Diet culture is a fear of death disguised as transformation.
sentences.zh: 减肥文化是伪装成蜕变的对死亡的恐惧。

sentences.en: But the transformation is a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 但这种蜕变是一种幻想。

sentences.en: If, through some heroic act of will, you do manage to heave yourself into a new place, it is still you who did the heaving.
sentences.zh: 如果通过某种英雄般的意志力，你确实设法把自己提升到了一个新的境界，那么进行这种提升的依然是你自己。

sentences.en: It is you who stands in the new place.
sentences.zh: 站在新境界里的依然是你。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You will still be you.
sentences.zh: 你依然会是你。

sentences.en: And I will still be Fat Sam.
sentences.zh: 而我依然会是胖山姆。

sentences.en: I will also be the person who is embarrassed by Fat Sam.
sentences.zh: 我也会是那个为胖山姆感到尴尬的人。

sentences.en: My feelings about my body form a chord of many notes, not all of which sound good together.
sentences.zh: 我对身体的感受构成了一个多音符的和弦，并非所有音符听起来都和谐。

sentences.en: I am, all at once, the one who wants to swallow the world and the one responsible for stopping myself from swallowing the world.
sentences.zh: 我既是那个想吞噬世界的人，也是那个负责阻止自己吞噬世界的人。

sentences.en: This probably means that I will always be unsatisfied in some way until the moment that everything ends.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着，在一切结束之前，我总会在某种程度上感到不满足。

sentences.en: And I will have to learn to be satisfied with this.
sentences.zh: 而我必须学会接受这种不满足。

sentences.en: For now, every morning, I wake up and try to direct Fat Sam within certain reasonable boundaries.
sentences.zh: 目前，每天早上醒来，我都会试着在一定的合理范围内引导胖山姆。

sentences.en: I make him a large bowl of Greek yogurt with green grapes and chopped fruits and 10 almonds.
sentences.zh: 我给他做了一大碗希腊酸奶，配上青葡萄、切碎的水果和10颗杏仁。

sentences.en: He eats it ravenously with hilarious joy.
sentences.zh: 他狼吞虎咽地吃着，带着滑稽的快乐。

sentences.en: Together, Fat Sam and I think about that yogurt for the rest of the day.
sentences.zh: 我和胖山姆整天都在惦记着那碗酸奶。

sentences.en: And we go to bed still thinking about it, excited to head down to the kitchen and eat it all again.
sentences.zh: 我们上床睡觉时还在想着它，期待着下楼去厨房再吃一次。

sentences.en: This story was written and narrated by Sam Anderson.
sentences.zh: 这个故事由萨姆·安德森（Sam Anderson）撰写并讲述。
